name: earthly
summary: Containerized build automation tool for reproducible, cache-aware, multi-target build pipelines.
why_it_matters: Earthly remains relevant capability knowledge for reproducible builds, but current Vrooli workflows do not rely on it enough to justify active maintenance.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs reproducible containerized builds across environments.
Operators want stronger build caching and target composition than ad hoc shell scripts provide.
The workflow needs BuildKit-oriented build definitions without full CI platform lock-in.

platform_support.notes: The CLI is broadly portable, but practical support depends on Docker or BuildKit availability and how Vrooli wants to model build ownership.

prerequisites: Clear ownership boundaries versus existing build scripts
implementation_notes: Future promotion should focus on validated build workflows instead of wrapping the entire Earthly command set.
Cache and artifact semantics should be defined before calling this supported.
Keep build orchestration distinct from deployment orchestration.
operational_notes: Version pinning and cache behavior materially affect reproducibility.
Build failures need surfaced logs and explicit artifact outputs.
Validation should exercise a known Earthfile rather than only checking the binary.
risks: Introducing another build abstraction can duplicate existing repo tooling.
Without a real consumer workflow, the wrapper would mostly preserve maintenance burden.
